_activity: Build the context sentence: the railway, 1830
intro: Build the sentence. Choose the right piece for each blank. This is the same starter your casefile uses.

tiles.text: Britain began digging canals in the 1760s to move coal more cheaply
the Liverpool and Manchester Railway opened
Britain had about 6,000 miles of railway
Manchester's mills still needed cotton through the port of Liverpool, and coal from the mines
one horse could pull a canal boat carrying about 30 tons
Adam Smith argued that dividing a job into small steps made workers more productive
a railway ran the 30 miles between the two cities
The Bridgewater Canal carried coal about 10 miles from the mines at Worsley to Manchester
Parliament passed thousands of enclosure acts

correct_sentence: After Britain began digging canals in the 1760s to move coal more cheaply, Manchester's mills still needed cotton through the port of Liverpool, and coal from the mines. By 1830, a railway ran the 30 miles between the two cities.
hints: The first blank is the thing that came BEFORE. The last blank is the document itself.
Two of the wrong tiles are true - they are just in the wrong place in time.
rationale: Context runs forward: the problem, then what was still true, then the thing in front of you. The tiles you left out are not false. 'The railway opened' and '6,000 miles' are the document and what came after it, and neither can explain what led to it.
